## Ecommerce Website Development in Pune: Should Your Store Integrate With ONDC in 2026?

If you're planning ecommerce website development in Pune in 2026, you've likely come across ONDC — the Open Network for Digital Commerce, India's government-backed attempt to do for online retail what UPI did for payments. The short answer to whether you should integrate with it is: probably yes, as an additional sales channel, but not as a replacement for having your own well-built ecommerce website. ONDC gives sellers a genuinely new way to be discovered across dozens of buyer apps without negotiating separate deals with each one, but it doesn't remove the need for a website you actually own, control, and can build a direct customer relationship through.

This guide explains what ONDC actually is, the real onboarding routes and costs, where it genuinely helps a Pune business, and where its limitations mean it should sit alongside your own website rather than instead of it — along with the practical, month-by-month shape of what onboarding actually involves, so you're evaluating it against a realistic picture rather than either the hype or the scepticism you'll find in different corners of the internet.

## What Is ONDC, in Plain Terms

ONDC is an open-protocol network, launched by the Indian government in 2022 under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, that connects buyer-facing apps and seller-facing platforms through a shared, standardised set of rules — much like UPI created a common protocol that let any bank's app talk to any other bank's app for payments, rather than requiring a business to integrate separately with every single payment provider. In practice, this means a product listed once through a compatible seller platform can become discoverable across every buyer app connected to the network, without the seller needing a direct relationship or separate technical integration with each one.

The network has grown quickly. By 2026, ONDC has crossed 500 million cumulative transactions, with government figures putting registered sellers at over 3 lakh (300,000+), operating across more than 400 cities and towns and connected to over 100 buyer apps. The network has also expanded well beyond retail — it now covers food and beverage ordering, mobility and ride-hailing (with over a million drivers onboarded), financial services, and public transport ticketing, reportedly carrying around 80% of India's metro ticketing inventory and facilitating over 370,000 public transport trips a day across several cities.

## How ONDC Integration Actually Works: Three Routes

There isn't one single way to "join ONDC" — the practical routes differ significantly in cost, speed, and technical complexity.

| Route | How it works | Typical timeline | Typical cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Via a Seller Network Participant (SNP) | Sign up with an ONDC-certified platform (examples include Mystore, eSamudaay, and category-specific platforms like Petpooja for food service) that handles the technical integration for you; you manage your catalogue through their dashboard | 1–4 weeks | ₹0–₹50,000 setup, plus 1–3% per transaction |
| Via your existing ecommerce platform's ONDC plugin or module | If your store already runs on a platform that offers ONDC connectivity as an add-on, enable and configure it | Days to a few weeks, depending on catalogue readiness | Varies by platform; typically a smaller incremental cost on top of your existing platform fees |
| Direct network participant integration | Build your own connection to ONDC's published protocol specifications from scratch, becoming your own registered network participant | 3–5 months for a minimum viable integration, 6–12 months for a production-grade one | ₹5,00,000–₹25,00,000+ to build, plus ₹15,000–₹50,000/month in ongoing infrastructure |

For the overwhelming majority of Pune ecommerce businesses, the Seller Network Participant route is the sensible starting point — it gets you discoverable on the network without the cost and timeline of a direct protocol integration, which realistically only makes sense for large retailers or platforms planning to offer ONDC connectivity as a service to others.

## Does ONDC Replace the Need for Your Own Website? No — Here's Why

It's worth being direct about this, because the framing of ONDC as "India's answer to Amazon" leads some business owners to assume it removes the need for their own ecommerce site entirely. It doesn't, for a few concrete reasons:

- **ONDC is a discovery and distribution layer, not a storefront.** Even when integrated through a Seller Network Participant, what a customer interacts with is a buyer app's interface, not your brand's own site — you gain reach, but you don't control the browsing experience, layout, or checkout flow the way you do on your own website.
- **You don't own the customer relationship the same way.** A sale made through a buyer app on the ONDC network gives you less direct access to the customer's contact details, browsing behaviour, and repeat-purchase potential than a sale made through your own site, where you can capture their WhatsApp number, email, and account for direct remarketing.
- **Margins differ.** Your own website, once built, carries no per-transaction platform commission beyond payment gateway fees (typically around 2%) — a meaningfully different economics than any marketplace-style channel, ONDC included, where a Seller Network Participant's fee structure still takes a cut.
- **Brand control matters for repeat business.** A customer who buys through a buyer app on ONDC associates the experience partly with that app, not necessarily with your brand — building loyalty, a returning customer base, and word-of-mouth is considerably easier when the entire journey happens on a site that's unmistakably yours.

The realistic way to think about ONDC is as an additional, lower-friction distribution channel that expands your reach — genuinely valuable, especially for smaller sellers who couldn't otherwise afford to be listed across dozens of separate apps — rather than a substitute for the ecommerce website that remains your primary, owned sales and brand asset.

## Benefits of ONDC Integration for a Pune Ecommerce Business

- **Lower typical commission structures** than several large marketplace platforms, whose category-dependent commission rates are often meaningfully higher than the 1–3% transaction fees typical of an ONDC Seller Network Participant — though exact marketplace commission rates vary by category and change over time, so it's worth comparing current rates directly rather than assuming a fixed gap.
- **One integration, many buyer apps.** Rather than negotiating and technically integrating with each marketplace or delivery app separately, a single ONDC-compatible listing becomes discoverable across the network's 100+ connected buyer apps.
- **Fuller data ownership than a typical closed marketplace.** ONDC's open architecture is explicitly designed to avoid the kind of platform lock-in associated with closed marketplaces, giving sellers more visibility into and control over their own transaction and customer data than a fully closed marketplace model typically allows.
- **Reach into geographies and buyer apps** a small or mid-size Pune business realistically couldn't access through direct integration deals on its own.

## Limitations and Realistic Expectations

- **Discoverability isn't the same as guaranteed sales.** Being listed on the network doesn't automatically generate demand — product photography, pricing competitiveness, and catalogue quality still determine whether a listing actually converts, exactly as on any other channel.
- **Buyer app scale is still growing relative to established marketplaces.** While ONDC's transaction volume has grown quickly, individual buyer apps connected to the network generally still have smaller active user bases than the largest established ecommerce marketplaces, and this gap is narrowing but hasn't closed.
- **Logistics integration adds a layer of complexity.** ONDC includes logistics network participants that can be integrated for fulfilment, but coordinating catalogue, inventory, and delivery across a new channel is real operational work, not something that happens automatically the moment you sign up with a Seller Network Participant.
- **Registration prerequisites.** You'll need a valid GST registration, business bank account details, and a catalogue in a format the Seller Network Participant can ingest before onboarding can begin — see our [GST and legal compliance checklist for ecommerce websites](/blog/ecommerce-gst-compliance-checklist-india-2026) for what needs to be in place on the tax and invoicing side regardless of which channels you sell through.

## Which Kinds of Ecommerce Businesses Benefit Most From ONDC

Not every ecommerce business gets equal value from ONDC integration, and it's worth being realistic about where the fit is genuinely strong versus merely plausible:

- **Small and mid-size retailers who currently can't afford marketplace-style reach.** A local Pune business selling handicrafts, regional food products, or niche fashion that couldn't justify the negotiation and integration effort of listing on multiple large marketplaces separately gets a genuinely outsized benefit from one integration reaching many buyer apps at once.
- **Category-specific sellers whose niche is well represented on the network.** Food and beverage, given the network's early and heavy investment in that category through partners like Petpooja, tends to see faster, more mature integration support than some newer categories.
- **Businesses already selling successfully on their own website, looking to add incremental reach.** ONDC works best layered on top of operational maturity you've already built, not as a first channel for a business that hasn't yet nailed its own fulfilment and customer service basics.

Conversely, a business still working out core operational issues — inconsistent stock accuracy, slow order processing, unreliable delivery partners — is likely to find that adding ONDC as a channel multiplies those existing problems across a new set of customers and buyer apps, rather than solving anything. A useful gut-check before onboarding: if your existing website already handles order volume smoothly, with accurate stock levels and predictable fulfilment times, you're in a reasonable position to add ONDC as an incremental channel. If your team is still firefighting basic order accuracy on your existing site, that's the more urgent priority to fix first.

## A Worked Example: What Onboarding Might Look Like Month by Month

To make the Seller Network Participant route concrete: in a typical first month, a Pune retailer would select and register with an ONDC-certified SNP, prepare and upload a product catalogue (photos, descriptions, pricing, GST details), and complete any required bank account verification. In the second to fourth week, the SNP typically runs test transactions to confirm the listing appears correctly across a sample of connected buyer apps, and the seller reviews how orders will flow into their existing order management process. From roughly the second month onward, actual customer orders begin arriving through the network, and the real operational learning starts — refining which products perform well through ONDC-specific channels, tuning pricing or promotions for that audience, and integrating fulfilment more tightly if order volume justifies it. This is, in broad shape, not meaningfully different from onboarding onto any new sales channel — the technical integration is genuinely faster than building direct marketplace relationships from scratch, but the operational ramp-up still takes real time and attention.

## ONDC Beyond Retail: What the Wider Network Means for a Pune Business

It's worth knowing that ONDC's ambitions extend well past product retail, because the network effect this creates can matter for adjacent parts of a business. The same open-protocol approach now covers food and beverage ordering, ride-hailing and logistics (with over a million drivers reportedly onboarded), financial services discovery, and even metro and public transport ticketing in several cities. For a Pune business that also operates a restaurant, offers local delivery, or has any adjacent service touching these categories, the same underlying network infrastructure and Seller Network Participant relationships can extend across more than just a product catalogue — worth discussing with whoever manages your ONDC integration if your business has operations spanning more than one of these categories.

## A Practical Path: Website First, ONDC as an Additional Channel

For most Pune ecommerce businesses, the sensible sequence is to get a solid, fast, well-optimised ecommerce website live first — with reliable checkout, proper payment gateway integration, and increasingly, WhatsApp-based order updates and cart recovery (our guide on [WhatsApp Business API for ecommerce](/blog/whatsapp-business-api-ecommerce-website-pune-2026) covers that side in depth) — and treat ONDC integration as an incremental channel added once your catalogue, photography, and fulfilment process are already working reliably on your own site. Adding a new distribution channel before your core operations are stable tends to multiply operational strain rather than multiply sales; adding it once the fundamentals work is a genuinely low-risk way to extend reach.

## Returns, Refunds and Settlement: What Doesn't Change

One thing worth clarifying before onboarding: ONDC's protocol standardises how orders, cancellations and returns are communicated across the network, but it doesn't remove your responsibility for defining and honouring your own returns and refund policy, or for the underlying settlement of funds, which still runs through your chosen payment gateway or the Seller Network Participant's settlement mechanism, typically on similar T+1 to T+3 timelines as other online payment methods. A seller onboarding to ONDC still needs a clear, published returns policy, a working process for handling cancellations, and the same customer-service discipline any other sales channel requires — the network standardises the technical communication of these events across buyer and seller apps, not the underlying business commitment behind them.

## Questions to Ask Your Ecommerce Website Development Partner in Pune About ONDC

- Which onboarding route (Seller Network Participant, existing platform plugin, or direct integration) makes sense for your specific scale, and why?
- What's the realistic timeline and cost for getting your actual product catalogue live on the network, not just a generic estimate?
- How will ONDC-driven orders flow into your existing inventory and fulfilment process — as a separate manual channel, or genuinely integrated?
- Does your team have experience with an actual ONDC integration, or would this be a first attempt on your project?
- What's the plan if a specific Seller Network Participant underperforms or changes its fee structure — is there a realistic path to switch?
- How will ONDC-sourced orders be reflected in your returns policy, customer support workflow, and settlement reconciliation, so nothing falls through the cracks between systems?

## How We Approach This at Govindani Infotech

Our [ecommerce website development](/services/ecommerce) work starts from the same principle in this guide: build a fast, well-optimised, fully owned storefront first, with reliable checkout and WhatsApp-based customer communication built in from the start, and treat additional distribution channels like ONDC as a genuine extension of that foundation rather than a replacement for it. We evaluate ONDC integration case by case with clients based on their catalogue readiness, fulfilment capacity, and realistic sales potential from the channel, rather than recommending it as a default add-on for every project.
